label: prop:gram-matrix-h3-symbolic
title: The H_3(q) Hoefsmit-seminormal Gram matrix on the 6-element normal-form basis, with the Markov weight $z$ carried symbolically: its determinant factors so that the canonical weight $z = q^3/(q^2+1)$ is a root, hence the canonical Gram is singular with the three-strand $q$-antisymmetriser as its radical.
html:
Proposition. The H_3(q) Hoefsmit-seminormal Gram matrix on the 6-element normal-form basis, with the Markov weight z carried symbolically: its determinant factors so that the canonical weight z = q^3/(q^2+1) is a root, hence the canonical Gram is singular with the three-strand q-antisymmetriser as its radical.

Let q > 0 and let z denote the Markov weight, so that on the 6-element Gröbner–Shirshov normal-form basis (b_0, \dots, b_5) = (1, \sigma_0, \sigma_1, \sigma_0\sigma_1, \sigma_1\sigma_0, \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0) of H_3(q) the Markov trace takes the values \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i) = (1, z, z, z^2, z^2, hz^2 + z) with h = q - q^{-1}. Let G(q,z) be the Gram matrix G[i,j] = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j). Then:

  1. G(q,z) is symmetric and G[0,0] = 1, for every z.

  2. The determinant factors as

  \det G(q,z) \;=\; -\,\frac{(z-q)^5\,(qz+1)^5\,\bigl((q^2+1)z - q^3\bigr)\,
                              (q^3 z + qz + 1)}{q^8}.

  1. At the canonical Markov weight z = q^3/(q^2+1) the third factor vanishes identically in q. Hence \det G = 0 for every q; the form has rank 5, and its radical is spanned by (-q^3,\, q^2,\, q^2,\, -q,\, -q,\, 1) — the three-strand q-antisymmetriser \sum_i (-q^{-1})^{\ell_i} b_i up to scale, where \ell_i is the word length of b_i. In particular G is not positive definite.

  2. At the excised convention-C weight z = \sqrt{q}/(q+1) one has instead \det G \neq 0 whenever \sqrt{q} > 1. This contrast is retained deliberately: it is what identifies the vanishing in item 3 as a property of the canonical weight rather than of the Gram construction. Convention C is not available for use — see the convention-D ruling.
